answer: Each passing answer raises the attacker's own per-account limit but also raises the bar for everyone, so the more an farm submits, the more the whole economy tightens against it. This holds because a newly minted alias starts worthless, so the attacker must first farm credibility on each one before it can swing a verdict. In practice this means a farm must spend real resources on every single alias, and that per-identity cost is what keeps the network honest at scale. Consider a sonnet as the anchor of the cost. A summit stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a terrace holds...
